title: Corrections module: Clone, Heal and AI Remove
objective: Deliver an offline, non-destructive Clone/Heal baseline and an optional provider-agnostic AI Remove workflow with durable frozen results, user-controlled models and exact UI/API parity.
context_summary: Planning proposal, not implementation authorization. The roadmap excludes generative editing until the owner accepts the new scope. Clone/Heal can proceed independently. AI implementation builds on the implemented module capabilities framework in docs/design/module-capabilities.md: user-level settings, OS-store secrets, per-asset consent, pinned-URL resources, capability tasks on the one job table and derived artifacts collected when a catalog opens; no cross-file task IDs are used. The groundwork other groups hold for this plan is not done yet and starts with it: stage-boundary methods on the compiled render entries (rendering) with the repair stage, and generic path primitives (masking) with the brush work; activation is being removed until `local-runtime` has a consumer, which the local adapter brings back (capabilities). Per-tile input regions and candidates as bounded job results are this plan's own work, as each task's context says.

tasks.description: Resolve corrections behavior, repair-stage ordering and the owner decision gates.
extra_context: The roadmap still excludes generative editing pending the owner's review of this proposal (docs/plan.md, Not in scope); this is a proposal until the owner explicitly accepts the new scope.

Decide how RAW source-development changes invalidate a frozen AI result. The proposed policy fails render/sample/export explicitly until regeneration or removal. Exposure is Basic's on every kind and the RAW source development carries white balance only (docs/decisions.md, Source-kind controls), so the change in question is a white-balance change; Basic's colour stage would run after the repair stage and not stale a patch.

The stage model today: `EffectStage` (modules/descriptor.rs) runs source, pixel, colour, spatial, geometry and finish, and `ModuleRegistry::insertion_index` (modules/registry/placement.rs) places a new layer by its declared stage and `order` without moving stored layers. The pixel stage holds only the developer-only pixel proof's `Processing::PointReplace`, which makes a stack proxy-ineligible (`ModuleRegistry::proxy_eligible`, modules/registry/compile.rs). The owner decided that whether `PointReplace` seeds the repair primitive or is deleted is decided with the repair stage (docs/decisions.md, Post-consolidation review).
Remote-photo consent is per asset by the recorded module-capabilities default (docs/decisions.md, Module capabilities); this task confirms or changes it for Corrections.

tasks.description: Add the narrow repair stage and bounded regional processing primitive.
extra_context: Preserve stored layer order; no catalog migration or generalized graph. The owner thread plans but never rasterizes.
Answer every performance-rules checklist item for changes under crates.

The compiled render `Entry` (render.rs) has two stage-boundary kinds, `Resample` and `Spatial`, matched in about 30 places across render.rs, render/pipeline.rs, render/window.rs, render/linear.rs, render/entry.rs and modules/registry/compile.rs. The rendering group's stage-boundary methods (an input-stage query, point mapping, the rectangle read, materialising and one-point evaluation, generalising `SpatialEntry` in render/pipeline.rs) wait for this task and land first, so a repair boundary is one implementation rather than a new arm at each site.

Per-tile input regions are this task's own work; no other plan carries them. A spatial tile reads its output rectangle plus the operation's summed halo, refused past `MAX_SPATIAL_HALO` (512 px, modules/spatial.rs), in the 512 or 1024 px tiles `luxforge_raw::spatial_tile` picks, and a global estimate is at most `MAX_GLOBAL_BYTES` (4 KiB). A clone reads at an arbitrary source offset beyond any halo and a heal needs a per-patch solve larger than a global estimate, so the repair primitive declares the input region each tile reads and its solve's scratch, charged to the render context's `SpatialBudget` (256 MiB target) under the same reserve-before-allocate rule.

Render limits live in luxforge-raw's limits module (the `render-limits-home` repository rule), and a new rendering pass takes its own `luxforge_raw::RenderPass` with a parallel threshold measured for it (`parallel_pixels`). Render tiles run in the render's own batches on the shared pool; `luxforge_raw::refill_each` is the RAW development executor, not a render scheduler.

Proxy eligibility is decided per stage (`ModuleRegistry::proxy_eligible`): a pixel-stage layer is ineligible because it addresses content pixels, and a spatial one is eligible but approximate. The repair stage declares which it is, and a preview against the proxy is labelled approximate where its pixels differ.

tasks.description: Add a semantic brush-mask descriptor, desktop canvas overlay and API path schema.
extra_context: Pointer events remain desktop-only; API clients submit bounded stroke geometry, source coordinates and add/subtract operations directly.

The path primitives are still the mask brush's own. `path.rs` holds `PathCapture` (the host grid the desktop brush pushes one position at a time), `decimate`, `Stroke`, `StrokeId` and the content-addressed `StrokeTable`, whose commit write stores only the strokes it does not already know are stored (`store_strokes` in editor/catalog.rs, with `insert_stored`, `mark_stored` and `is_known_stored`). But `path.rs` imports `mask::{REFINE_MAX, REFINE_MIN}` for `ColourLimit` and takes `SIZE_MIN` from `mask::DISTANCE_MIN`, `Recipe::stroke_references` (model.rs) finds strokes in mask components only, `Draft.target` (draft.rs) is an optional `MaskTarget`, and the desktop brush (`mask_draft/brush.rs`) drives `mask.add-stroke` alone. The masking group's generic path primitives (consumer-declared stroke types in the one store, draft targets from declared identity parameters) wait for this work and land first.

The descriptor's canvas interactions are `point-pick`, `sample-apply` and `crop-frame` (`CanvasInteraction`, modules/descriptor.rs); the mask brush is the host's `mask.*` command family, not a declared interaction. Stroke geometry is the `points` parameter kind, refused past `POSTED_POINTS_PER_STROKE` before decimation and `POINTS_PER_STROKE` (1,024) after, with a radius-relative decimation tolerance. A component-kind token is named only in the host's kind table (`mask/mod.rs`), each kind's file and the desktop's drawn-kind table (the `component-kind` repository rule), so a corrections brush declares its own stroke type rather than reusing the mask brush kind.

tasks.description: Implement the corrections module's ordered Clone/Heal operations and edit actions.
extra_context: One layer holds stable operation IDs; actions add, update, remove and reorder operations without module-owned catalog writes.

Every mutating action carries the `{request_id, actor}` envelope and `expected_revision`, checked once in the dispatcher (`Envelope::check`, api/params.rs), and a module supplies its history label through `ToolModule::label()`. The `identity` parameter kind is host-only today (`ParameterKind::host_only`), so a module-owned operation ID either uses another kind or waits for the generic path primitives' identity parameters.
acceptance_criteria: The module owns validated stroke/source payloads and compiles ordered Clone/Heal operations through the host primitive; all actions appear in schema.list.
Each successful operation changes one ordinary history entry; no-op, wrong operation ID, bad source and stale mutation have explicit outcomes.
Changing a crop or orientation carries corrections in content space; source development recomputes Clone/Heal rather than silently freezing pixels.

tasks.description: Integrate immutable AI repair patches, mask composition and prefix invalidation.
extra_context: Builds on the implemented derived artifacts (docs/design/module-capabilities.md, Derived artifacts): a task publishes content-addressed bytes through `ModuleContext::publish_artifact` (at most 16 per task, 256 MiB each), an effect declaring `artifacts: true` lists them on its layer, the commit checks each has a row and a file, evaluation binds them into the recipe (`EditorService::bind_artifacts`) and `CapabilityModule::compile_bound` receives the bytes. A missing or corrupt artifact fails render, sample, analysis and export with `source-unavailable`.
Rendering uses a frozen host-owned patch and never invokes its generation provider.

A task's result today is its JSON plus the IDs of the artifacts it published, and every published artifact stays until a collection finds it unreferenced: opening a catalog queues one collection on the source worker, and `artifact.collect` skips artifacts a task of the current process published. Disposable multi-megabyte candidates therefore need a bounded job result that is not an artifact, read through `job.read`, with only the accepted patch published; that result shape is this task's work.
`spatial::prefix_hash` (render/spatial.rs) already hashes a layer prefix with the masks it reads, including their sampling, which is the input-prefix identity a frozen patch needs.

tasks.description: Implement a qualified downloadable local inference adapter when its candidate passes.
extra_context: If qualification rejects all local models, complete this task only by recording a no-go with evidence and keep local AI unavailable; do not substitute an unreviewed model.

Generic download, settings and permissions are implemented: a resource installs only from its pinned URL under the `download-artifact` grant, checked by length, SHA-256 and the module's `validate_resource` hook, and a task reads it through `ModuleContext::resource_path`. Capability tasks run on the one job table's `module` lane, one thread with at most four queued.

Activation (`module.activate`, `module.deactivate`, `JobKind::Activate`/`Deactivate`, capabilities/host/activation.rs) is being removed until a module needs `local-runtime` (docs/decisions.md, Post-consolidation review). This adapter is that first consumer and brings back activation and `local-runtime` together, preloading a model with a cancellable worker off the owner thread; downloaded weights are never loaded through a general object deserializer.

tasks.description: Implement typed remote AI adapters and provider selection.
extra_context: Requires generic settings, secret storage, network permission and jobs, which the module capabilities framework implements: settings use the module parameter vocabulary, secrets live only in the OS credential store (the macOS Keychain first), and a task is a capability job read and cancelled through `job.read` and `job.cancel`. First live providers are chosen in the qualification task.
Do not pass original paths, EXIF or extra image bytes by default.

The transport runs on `ureq`'s own agent (`capabilities/transport/`) behind the unchanged address policy, and the `http-framing` repository rule keeps HTTP framing inside it; the capabilities group moves the transport and the secret store into their own crate, injected through `HostConfig`. At the 1,024-record grant cap (`MAX_GRANT_RECORDS`) the oldest live remote-image grant is evicted, so per-asset consent keeps working. Remote-photo consent is per asset by the recorded default; the decision task confirms or changes that before the first adapter ships.

tasks.description: Add AI Remove mask refinement, candidate review and atomic acceptance to the Corrections UI/API.
extra_context: A local no-go in TASK-009 does not block an accepted remote AI delivery; candidate acceptance rechecks revision and prefix before commit.

The target mask is a draft on the core `draft.*` lifecycle: `draft.begin`, `draft.set`, `draft.cancel` and `draft.reapply` run synchronously on the desktop thread and `draft.commit` as an owner task, and Undo, Redo and Restore are refused while a draft is open (docs/decisions.md, Post-consolidation review). Events name the asset and revision they changed, so a late candidate is recognisable as stale.
